grammarFocus: 关系从句；指代；可能性表达；复杂句主干辨认。
title: The Library of Lost Sounds
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章为模拟教育材料，非官方雅思试题。题目类型包括单选、填空、匹配（以单选形式）和判断正误/未提及。填空答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有解释为中文，证据为英文原文引用。
passage:
In the small town of Marlow, there is a library that does not lend books. It lends sounds. The Marlow Sound Library, which was founded by a retired music teacher named Eleanor Voss, contains hundreds of recordings of everyday noises: the clatter of a blacksmith’s hammer, the whistle of a steam train, the creak of a wooden windmill. Visitors can borrow a recording for a week, listen to it at home, and then return it. The library has no fines, because, as Eleanor says, “A sound that is late is still a sound.”

Eleanor started the collection in 1985, when she realised that many of the sounds she had grown up with were disappearing. The factory where her father worked had closed, and its machines had been sold for scrap. The railway station had been modernised, and the old announcement bell had been replaced by a digital voice. “I wanted to keep something,” she explains. “Not a photograph, which shows only what things looked like, but a recording, which shows what they sounded like.” She began by borrowing a tape recorder from a friend and walking around the town, asking people if she could record their workplaces. Some were suspicious, but most agreed. Within a year, she had collected over two hundred sounds.

The library is housed in a converted chapel, which Eleanor bought with her savings. The building has thick stone walls, which keep the recordings cool and dry. Inside, there are shelves of cassette tapes, reel-to-reel tapes, and, more recently, digital files. Each recording is labelled with the date, the place, and the name of the person who made it. Eleanor insists that every recording must include the permission of the people whose voices or workplaces are captured. “It’s not just about the sound,” she says. “It’s about the people who made it.”

Not everyone understands the library’s purpose. A local councillor once asked why the town should spend money on “old noises” when there were more urgent needs. Eleanor replied that the library was not a museum of nostalgia but a resource for the future. “If we don’t know what the past sounded like,” she argued, “we can’t understand how much our environment has changed.” She pointed out that the library is used by researchers, artists, and even doctors who study hearing loss. A group of students from the local school recently used recordings of a busy market to create a soundscape for a play about the town’s history.

The library’s most popular recording is of a bell that once hung in the town hall. The bell was rung every hour until 1972, when it was removed because it was cracked. For years, people forgot about it. Then, in 2010, a local historian found a tape of the bell in the library’s collection. The tape had been made by a teenager in 1968, who had recorded it as a school project. When the recording was played at a town meeting, several older residents began to cry. “It was the sound of my childhood,” one of them said. The bell itself has never been repaired, but the recording has become a kind of substitute, which the town uses at special events.

Eleanor, who is now in her seventies, still visits the library every day. She is training a group of volunteers, who will take over when she retires. “I’m not worried about the future,” she says. “The sounds will outlive me. What matters is that people keep listening.” The library receives no government funding; it relies on donations and on the small fees that visitors pay to borrow recordings. Eleanor believes that this independence is important, because it allows the library to keep all its recordings, even those that some people might find unpleasant. “A sound doesn’t have to be beautiful to be worth keeping,” she says. “It just has to be true.”

grammar.title: 关系从句与复杂句主干辨认
grammar.explanation: 关系从句用who, which, that等引导，修饰前面的名词。在复杂句中，先找到主句的主语和谓语，再分析从句。例如：'The library, which was founded by Eleanor, contains recordings.' 主句是'The library contains recordings'，'which was founded by Eleanor'是关系从句。
grammar.example: The Marlow Sound Library, which was founded by a retired music teacher named Eleanor Voss, contains hundreds of recordings of everyday noises.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: The man ___ recorded the bell was a teenager.
questions.explanation: 先行词是the man，指人，关系代词在从句中作主语，用who。
questions.evidence: The tape had been made by a teenager in 1968, who had recorded it as a school project.

questions.prompt: Identify the main clause: 'The library, which Eleanor bought with her savings, has thick stone walls.'
options: The library has thick stone walls.
which Eleanor bought with her savings
answers: The library has thick stone walls.
questions.explanation: 主句是'The library has thick stone walls'，关系从句'which Eleanor bought with her savings'修饰the library。
questions.evidence: The building has thick stone walls, which keep the recordings cool and dry.

questions.prompt: Combine: 'The bell was cracked. It was removed.' Use a relative clause.
options: The bell, which was cracked, was removed.
The bell was cracked, it was removed.
The bell which was cracked it was removed.
The bell was cracked which was removed.
answers: The bell, which was cracked, was removed.
questions.explanation: 非限制性关系从句用which引导，前后加逗号。
questions.evidence: The bell was rung every hour until 1972, when it was removed because it was cracked.

questions.prompt: What does 'who' refer to in: 'She is training a group of volunteers, who will take over when she retires.'?
questions.explanation: 关系代词who指代前面的a group of volunteers。
questions.evidence: She is training a group of volunteers, who will take over when she retires.
